runs.reason:

The reported launch totals, in order, were 141, 98, about 400, 148, 186, 153, and 96. That’s a 43% recent base rate, though seven nights is a small sample. **What moves the estimate:** The November 22 and 23 reports, at 186 and 153, nudge the forecast toward YES: neither needed a barrage on the scale of November 20 to clear the threshold. The latest report, at 96 on November 24, pulls the other way. I give these mixed signals little weight beyond the base rate and lean slightly NO. ([ukrinform.ua](https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-ato/4187285-ppo-zneskodila-161-zi-186-bezpilotnikiv-akimi-rosiani-z-vecora-atakuvali-ukrainu.html?utm_source=openai))

**Window risk:** All seven comparison nights had reported launches, so I give little weight to the possibility of no launches at all in the November 25–26 window. The main route to NO is a first summary reporting 149 or fewer. A summary published after noon Kyiv time on November 26 can still count; an absent summary leaves the claim pending. ### (3) Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail

While a probability slightly above 50% favors YES due to the high monthly base rate and Zelensky's 23 November warning of impending strikes, this could easily fail if Russia executes its prepared large-scale strike a day earlier (on the night of 24–25 November), which in recent cycles (such as Nov 19–20's 404 drones followed by Nov 20–21's 148 drones) typically leaves the subsequent night just below the 150-drone mark. Additionally, Russia sometimes splits its daily UAV launches between overnight and daytime waves (as seen on 10 and 12 November, when separate daytime summaries accounted for 143–155 drones), or weather conditions and tactical shifts toward front-line/border infrastructure (like the 96-drone attack focused on Zhytomyr on 23–24 November) could keep the overnight total in the 95–148 range. (The chance that no summary is published or no attack happens in the window is negligible, as the Air Force has published an overnight summary every day this month).

Balancing the 50%–61% base rate with the pending intelligence warning of a new strike (+5%) and the uncertainty over whether a spike lands on 24–25 Nov versus 25–26 Nov, I forecast a **0.56** probability of YES.

runs.reason:
Recent overnight Russian UAV salvos against Ukraine, as counted in the Air Force’s morning summaries, have varied widely but clustered mostly between roughly 90 and 190, with occasional much larger waves.

Base rate: across a dozen consecutive nights in mid-to-late November 2026 for which the first Air Force totals are published, about 40–50 percent reached 150 or more UAVs (including Shahed-type, jet-powered variants, Gerbera, Parodiya and any munitions the summary folds into the UAV figure). Massive combined barrages above 300 occur but are infrequent (roughly one or two per fortnight). Zero-drone nights and missing summaries are essentially unobserved in this period, so the claim turns almost entirely on whether the 25–26 November total clears 150.

Facts shifting the case: the most recent published nights show the same spread (96, 153, 186, 148), so the short-term run rate sits near the threshold rather than clearly above or below it. A 23 November statement that intelligence indicated preparations for further strikes is consistent with the ongoing campaign but supplies no size or date.

The distribution’s center of mass for ordinary nights lies a little under 150, and nothing dated points to a specially large salvo on the night of 25–26 November in particular.
